title: LFU Cache
summary: Implement a cache with get(key) and put(key,value).

contractDetails.constraints: 1 ≤ capacity ≤ 10000. Keys are in [0,100000], values in [0,1000000000]. At most 200000 calls. Rows [0,key,value] call put and [1,key] call get. Construct once. Serialize only get results.
contractDetails.output-checking: Construct LFUCache(capacity) once. Dispatch 0=put(key,value) and 1=get(key). Serialize only get returns. get and updates increase frequency. Eviction uses frequency then least recent use.

statement: Implement a cache with get(key) and put(key,value). get returns −1 for a missing key. A new key starts with use count one. A successful get or an update of an existing key increases its use count by one. When a new key needs space, evict the stored key with the smallest use count. Break ties by evicting the least recently used key. Each method must run in O(1) average time.

examples.explanation: Using key 1 protects it from eviction.
Updating an existing key changes its value and frequency.
Equal frequencies evict the least recently used key.

constraints: 1 ≤ capacity ≤ 10000. Keys are in [0,100000], values in [0,1000000000]. At most 200000 calls. Rows [0,key,value] call put and [1,key] call get. Construct once. Serialize only get results.
hints: Conceptual: Eviction needs both a frequency and a recency rule.
Directional: Group keys with equal frequency in recency order.
Implementation: Keep a map to each key’s node, a linked list per frequency, and the smallest active frequency. Move a touched key to the next frequency list.
complexityAnalysis: O(1) average time per get and put. O(C+U+T) storage for the direct-address internal reference, where C is capacity, U is the key domain, and T bounds frequency levels. A hash-map implementation needs O(C) storage.
